replace.find: For a permanent production deployment, a small Linux VPS with 1 vCPU and 1 GB RAM is sufficient for a few thousand voters. The recommended server stack is nginx or Apache with PHP-FPM, a managed MySQL 8/MariaDB 10.6+ instance, TLS termination with a valid certificate, and nightly backups of both the database and data/secret.key. A lighter-weight permanent address is also supported: a named Cloudflare tunnel maps a hostname on a Cloudflare-managed domain to this machine without opening an inbound port. The application itself needs no code changes; only the DB_* environment variables and the web-server document root change.
replace.with: For permanent production hosting the project ships a Dockerfile and a Render Blueprint. Render runs the PHP application on its free web tier with a managed HTTPS subdomain, and Neon provides a free PostgreSQL database that does not expire. All secrets are supplied through environment variables (DB_DRIVER, DB_HOST, DB_PORT, DB_NAME, DB_USER, DB_PASS, ADMIN_EMAIL, ADMIN_PASSWORD and APP_URL). The schema and seed administrator are created automatically on first boot. A named Cloudflare tunnel remains available for local demonstrations, and the same PHP code can also be deployed on a small VPS behind nginx or Apache with PHP-FPM.

replace.with: The system is organised into a presentation layer, an application layer and a data layer. The browser renders a single-page application with real path-based URLs built from a reusable component library and communicates with the server only through JSON endpoints (also published as /api/v1 with an OpenAPI 3.1 specification). The server returns an HTML shell for deep links with noscript content for crawlers, while per-route metadata keeps titles, canonical URLs and social cards accurate. The PHP front controller authenticates the session, validates requests through a central validator, and executes business rules before reading or writing the database through a driver-aware PDO layer that supports both PostgreSQL and MariaDB. This separation keeps the security decisions on the server and makes the client replaceable.

replace.find: All application data is stored in a relational MariaDB database. The schema uses InnoDB, the utf8mb4 character set and UTC DATETIME(3) timestamps so that the application, the database and the browser agree on time. Foreign keys protect the relationships between elections, candidates, votes and audit entries, and unique constraints enforce the rules that must not depend on the user interface.
replace.with: All application data is stored in a relational database: PostgreSQL in production and MariaDB for local development. The schema uses UTF-8 text and UTC millisecond timestamps so that the application, the database and the browser agree on time. Foreign keys protect the relationships between elections, candidates, votes and audit entries, unique constraints enforce the rules that must not depend on the user interface, and a parallel schema.pgsql file keeps the two drivers in sync.

replace.find: The database contains seven tables. The votes table deliberately has no foreign key to users and no timestamp: it stores the election, the candidate and a keyed receipt hash. A separate participation table records who voted and when, with a unique key that enforces one ballot per voter. The audit_log table stores the actor, the action, JSON details and the IP address.

Additional tables support e-mail verification, password resets, TOTP challenges, rate limiting, one-time backup codes, WebAuthn passkeys and their challenges, webhooks, notifications, and Merkle roots for published ballots.

replace.with: Free-tier hosting has trade-offs. The production site runs on Render's free web service with a Neon PostgreSQL database and is available 24/7, but the free web service sleeps after inactivity and Neon suspends after five minutes of idle time; a free uptime monitor keeps both awake. There is no failover or load balancing, and custom domains require a domain the institution owns.

lines: Enhancements delivered in the second phase are also in scope. The front end now has a token-based design system, a reusable component library, a light theme, a living style guide at #/design, and a service worker with an installable PWA manifest.

Account security includes WebAuthn passkeys, ten single-use backup codes, TOTP multi-factor authentication, signed audit export, and passwordless sign-in. Election administration gained a tabbed election manager, election cloning, CSV candidate import, turnout analytics, notifications and configurable webhooks.

Verifiability was extended with a SHA-256 Merkle tree of ballot receipt hashes, inclusion proofs returned by the verification endpoint, a public audit endpoint, and a live entity-relationship diagram generated from the database catalogue.

lines: Database portability is handled in src/php/db.php: DB_DRIVER selects the mysql or pgsql DSN, DB_SSLMODE controls TLS (required by Neon in production), and driver-specific helpers cover introspection, duplicate-key detection and SQL dialect differences. The connection is recreated after schema migrations so PostgreSQL discards cached query plans whose result types changed.
